clue.text: Public anger becomes excessively weary

parts.note: something public is open and overt
ire is an old word for anger

explanation.surface: Public fury leaves someone utterly exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtire is to grow far more fatigued than is good for you, as a verb used intransitively.

clue.text: Business is now hotting up

definitions.meaning: a place of business, or a firm's premises
read as ...: something just taken ... is warming up

explanation.definitionFit: A business works from an office; food removed from the ice store is off ice and so warming.

clue.text: Upset about a piece of jewel, lery going astray

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the short word for about upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone distraught over a lost piece of jewellery that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Upset' turns the short word upside down, so it reads from the bottom; 'Upset' in the surface looks like distress over lost jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means wandering from the right path, so it is a synonym of straying.

clue.text: Essays he has written in the Times Educational Supplement

indicators.note: words written in a publication sit inside its name, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TES is the usual abbreviation of the Times Educational Supplement, a UK teachers' weekly
he has contracts to he's

explanation.surface: A teacher has contributed essays to a newspaper for educators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' is the container signal. The Times Educational Supplement is a British weekly paper for teachers, known by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Theses are long academic dissertations, a kind of formal essay.

clue.text: Commercial traveller is given a fixed allowance as compensation

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman receives a set allowance to make up for his costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation is amends or payment made for a wrong or loss, so it is a synonym of compensation.

clue.text: Child takes a look in the lounge-bar

indicators.note: the child piece takes the other pieces inside it, so they sit within it

parts.note: a son is a child
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: A child peers into the lounge bar of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is the container signal. In British pubs the saloon bar is the more comfortable room, also called the lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: The saloon, or saloon bar, is the better-furnished room of a British pub, also called the lounge.

clue.text: Famous warrior awarded a high place among the experts

indicators.note: the high place is set among the experts, inside that word

parts.note: aces are experts
a hill is a high place

explanation.surface: A celebrated soldier is given an elevated position among the masters of his craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is the container signal; 'awarded' is only a link, though it tempts as part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero of the Trojan War is the most famous fighter in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Disregarding an appeal to the embassy

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: An official request to a foreign embassy goes ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a leaving out or neglect, used here as the noun sense of disregarding.

clue.text: Legal officials born between 21st April and 20 th March

definitions.meaning: public officers who certify documents and oaths

definitions.text: born between 21st April and 20 th March
definitions.meaning: anyone born outside the 21 March to 20 April star sign

explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are lawyers who witness deeds; split as NOT ARIES they are people of any other star sign.

clue.text: Always a supporter of mediaeval fortresses

parts.note: someone for a cause supports it
a keep is the central tower of a medieval castle

explanation.surface: A lifelong fan of old castles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given for keeps is given permanently, so the phrase means forever.

clue.text: The first man to believe in God

parts.note: first is abbreviated 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Adam, the very first human, was a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Adam; the definition is the clue's last five words.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is a person who holds that a deity exists.

clue.text: A bomber reaches the centre of Australian government

definitions.meaning: the English Electric jet bomber of the 1950s

explanation.definitionFit: The Canberra was a British jet bomber, named after Australia's capital, the seat of its parliament.

clue.text: He concludes it's not so far off

definitions.meaning: one who finishes or seals something, like a relief pitcher who ends a game

explanation.definitionFit: A closer is one who brings matters to an end; closer is also the comparative adjective meaning nearer.

clue.text: Abduction of a sleeping child

parts.note: a kid is a child
napping means dozing or sleeping

explanation.surface: A sleeping infant is snatched.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an abduction; the wordplay is the plain picture of a dozing child.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapping is the unlawful carrying off of a person, the same crime as abduction.

clue.text: Attack the family unit just to make a point

parts.note: to strike is to attack
a home is where a family lives together

explanation.surface: Someone assaults their own household merely to prove something.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike home is to have the intended effect, as an argument that lands with force.

clue.text: I am going into property valuation

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: an estate is landed property
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone is off to get a house valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' is the container signal, and 'property' tempts as the definition, but the definition is 'valuation' at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate judgement of worth, so it is a synonym of valuation.

clue.text: Freelance typist not arriving punctually — and it's a pattern

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker such as a typist
late means after the expected time

explanation.surface: An agency typist turns up late again, and it has become a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pattern' looks like a habit of lateness in the surface; it is the guide shape that defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a shaped guide used to copy a design, so it is a pattern.

clue.text: To have a rookie taking up weapons is frightening

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
arming means equipping with or taking up arms

explanation.surface: Seeing a raw recruit take up arms is a scary thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes sudden fear, so it is a synonym of scary.

clue.text: Charmed by tour of duty before the spring

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a spell is a period of work or duty
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Enchanted by a stint of service just ahead of springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spellbound is held as if by magic, so it is a synonym of enchanted.

clue.text: The way in exercise to acquire a heavenly body

indicators.note: the way is put in the exercise, inside it

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise
a lane is a narrow way or road

explanation.surface: Joining a route in gym class to reach the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. PT, physical training, is the British school name for gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a large body orbiting a star, one of the heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Jack needs to become objective

parts.note: jack tar and tar are old names for a sailor
to get, as in 'get wet', is to become

explanation.surface: A man called Jack must learn to be impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objective' looks like the adjective meaning impartial; it is the noun meaning an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is an aim, and a target is the goal one aims at.

clue.text: Recovered his gambling expenses, did he?

definitions.text: Recovered his gambling expenses, did he?

parts.words: Recovered his gambling expenses, did he?
parts.note: one who places wagers and wins back his stake is also improved, back on form after illness

explanation.surface: A punter asks whether a gambler got his money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recovered' means healed, as after an illness; the question describes a person who places wagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who wagers is a bettor, spelt this way too, and someone who has recovered from illness is said to be well again.

clue.text: Putting on an act, to some ex tent

explanation.definitionFit: An actor in a role is playing a part; the same phrase means partly or not wholly.

clue.text: The wise man swallows medicine in liquid drops

indicators.note: the wise man swallows the medicine, taking it inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: An old wise man takes a tablet with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' is the container signal; 'drops' reads as a dose of medicine but is a noun meaning drips.
explanation.definitionFit: Spillage is fluid that has been spilt, the drips that fall.

clue.text: First-class graduate and painter return from Middle-Eastern countries

indicators.note: return turns the whole string of pieces round so it reads backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the figure read as I
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A top graduate and an artist come home from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: AIBARA read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabia is the peninsula holding Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman and their neighbours, a group of nations.

clue.text: Twelve hiding-places in Montana

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for Montana

indicators.note: places, as a verb, means puts the letters in new positions

explanation.surface: A dozen hideouts somewhere in Montana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container one. 'hiding-places' reads as one word, but the hyphen splits fodder from indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour of twelve at night is the middle of the night.

clue.text: Green organisation has a yen for power

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An environmental group is keen to take political power.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy is the capacity to do work, the physicist's sense of power.

clue.text: Single soldier at Teignmouth gets the first eighteen letters from a rabble-rouser

parts.note: a means one, single
a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: the first of the Devon town's name is its opening letter

parts.note: the first eighteen letters of the alphabet run A to R

explanation.surface: A lone soldier in a Devon seaside town receives a pile of letters from a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first' takes T, the opening letter of Teignmouth (a Devon seaside town); 'eighteen letters' gives A TO R, the alphabet's first eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up crowds to protest, a synonym of a demagogue.
